title: Flip window anchoring and safe-handoff notebook
body:
Context:
- Personal scratchpad for a late-night flip where we need to anchor a model/version and hand off to on-call. Not a formal playbook, more of a quick operational memory aid.
- Target: flip hosted text-generation model v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0-lite (quantized) during quiet window. Keep pinned fallbacks.

High-level goals:
1) Minimize user-facing latency regressions.
2) Keep cost delta visible and bounded during first 4h.
3) Be ready to roll back within 10 minutes if error/safety signals spike.

Known constraints:
- Night window: 02:00-06:00 PST (low traffic).
- Canary cohort limited to 0.5% of traffic initial, up to 8% if green.
- Dedicated cached buckets exist for top-500 tenants—do NOT include them in this canary unless explicit.

Quick checklist (pre-flip):
- [ ] Confirm model artifacts deployed to all regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1) and checksum matches release tag.
- [ ] Verify fallback variants pinned: v2.3.1 and v2.2.9 (safety pin).
- [ ] Confirm routing rules in infra-config PR (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Run smoke queries (3 prompts) across regions and compare token counts and latencies; capture traces.
- [ ] Ensure canary quota limits set (0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8%) with 15–30m observation windows.
- [ ] Alert page ready: short runbook + who to page (on-call + release lead).

Telemetry/Signals to watch (fast list):
- Latency P95 and P99 for text.generate per region (baseline and canary): alert if +30% P95 or +50% P99.
- Error rate: 5xx and model-level errors (decode failures). Alert if >0.3% absolute increase vs baseline or >1.0% in canary cohort.
- Failure modes: OOMs, VMM spikes, OOM kills on host. If kernel OOMs seen, immediate rollback.
- Safety classifier rate (if available): proportion of responses flagged. Alert if >0.2% absolute increase.
- Token cost per call: watch mean tokens * cost-per-token; alert if extra cost >15% sustained for 30m.
- User-visible regressions: SLO of 99.5% success on short-completion (responses <3s).

Quick metric queries (examples to paste into console):
- Latency by cohort: SELECT cohort, percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95, percentile(latency_ms,99) as p99 FROM request_metrics WHERE model IN ('v2.3.1','v2.4.0-lite') AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY cohort;
- Error rate: SELECT cohort, sum(is_error)::float / count(*) FROM request_metrics WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY cohort;
- Safety flags: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE safety_flag = true) / count(*) FROM responses WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes';

Initial rollout plan (rapid but cautious):
- T0: set routing rule -> 0.5% global traffic, keep pinned fallback. Observe 20m.
- T0+20m: if all green, bump to 1.5% (observe 25m).
- T0+45m: bump to 3% (observe 30m).
- T1+1h15m: bump to 6% (observe 30m).
- T1+1h45m: bump to 8% and hold for 2h before broader rollout.
Notes: stop and hold at any step if any alert triggers. Always wait for full observation window.

Anchoring strategy (why pinned fallbacks matter):
- Keep v2.3.1 pinned in routing table for instant fallback. Do not remove it until the 8% hold completes and post-8h checks are green.
- Maintain metadata: a specific tag in routing config that marks 'anchor=true' for fallback. That allows automated rollback via routing key.

Rollback decision tree (fast):
1) Safety classifier spike or content regression reported by TA -> immediate rollback to pinned v2.3.1, notify product safety.
2) Latency P95 > +30% sustained for 10m -> pause rollouts and if persists 15m -> rollback.
3) Error rate absolute increase >0.3% vs baseline in canary -> rollback.
4) Infrastructure-level failures (OOM, host evictions) -> rollback immediately and open infra incident.
5) Cost spike >15% sustained 30m -> pause and evaluate; rollback if cannot be mitigated.

Rollback steps (short):
- In routing console: flip 'model.active' routing key to v2.3.1 anchor.
- Confirm traffic shift in metrics (should reflect near-immediate reversion).
- Page on-call + release lead via standard incident template.
- Keep canary config frozen and add postmortem notes in linked Artifacts (JIRA ticket).

Communication templates (short messages to send):
- To #release-ops: "Flipping canary -> v2.4.0-lite at 02:15 PST (0.5%). Observing latency/error/safety for 20m. Will post updates every bump or on alert. Owner: @izhang. On-call: @marcod."
- If rollback: "ROLLED BACK: v2.4.0-lite -> v2.3.1 at 02:47 PST due to latency spike. Rollback executed; monitoring for residual issues. Incident ticket: ENG-2789."

Post-flip short checklist (first 4 hours):
- [ ] Confirm long-tail latencies normalized (P99 within threshold).
- [ ] Check for regressions in quality by sampling 50 random responses across cohorts.
- [ ] Cost delta review after 1h and 4h.
- [ ] Mark rollout status on Confluence and close temporary routing flag.

Open questions / things to log while on-call:
- Which tenants were routed into the canary by cohort selection? (log list)
- Any correlated increase in cache miss rate? (important for token cost)
- Were there any out-of-band infra events at the host/container level?

Personal notes / heuristics (biases called out):
- If the canary is slower but errors and safety are equal, prefer to keep and investigate quantization knobs — latency-only problems can be mitigated without rollback in some cases.
- If safety or content regressions are reported even once by human reviewer, roll back immediately. No negotiation.

TODO (action items to do right now before leaving):
- [ ] Push small smoke-validation script to /ops/tools/rollout-smoke.sh and verify it runs in CI.
- [ ] Create the quick dashboard with the three top signals (latency, errors, safety) and share link in Slack.
- [ ] Confirm on-call rotation for the window and add me @izhang as secondary contact.

End-of-note: keep this as my ephemeral brain dump. If anything becomes stable, move to the canonical playbook in Confluence.
